extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry and number theory, especially readers studying Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmüller theory (IUT)
extracted.subtask_description: A detailed, self-contained survey exposition of Shinichi Mochizuki's inter-universal Teichmüller theory and how it gives rise to Diophantine inequalities (in particular Vojta-type inequalities and the abc conjecture). The document lays out reduction steps, required background, constructions (log-volumes, theta-functions, Frobenioids, Hodge theatres), and the final multiradial algorithm leading to height bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 0.1 (Vojta's Conjecture for Curves)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be a proper, smooth, geometrically connected curve over a number field; D ⊂ X a reduced divisor; U_X := X \ D. Suppose U_X is hyperbolic (deg(ω_X(D)) > 0). Then for any d ∈ Z_{>0} and ε ∈ R_{>0} we have ht_{ω_X(D)} . (1 + ε)(log-diff_X + log-cond_D) on U_X(Q)^{d}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as a consequence of IUT; the theorem is the primary Diophantine inequality one aims to establish and is the key input to derive the abc corollary. The survey indicates how later constructions (multiradial algorithm, log-volumes, Hodge-Arakelov evaluation, log-links) are combined to prove this inequality. See Section 1. (Scoring/verification: check height inequality holds up to bounded error; applicability requires hyperbolicity and the arithmetic setup described.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 0.2 (The abc Conjecture)
rubrics_metrics.description: From Theorem 0.1 one deduces the abc Conjecture (Masser–Oesterlé): for any ε > 0, max(|a|,|b|,|c|) ≲ ∏_{p|abc} p^{1/(1+ε)} for all but finitely many coprime integer triples a+b=c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The corollary is obtained by applying Theorem 0.1 to X = P^1_Q with D = {0,1,∞} and standard height/log-conductor computations. The proof sketch explains how choice of ε and normalization yield the classical abc inequality up to finitely many exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction via General Arithmetic Geometry (Section 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce the main Diophantine inequality (Theorem 0.1) to a specific inequality involving log-q and log(⋯) terms; reduction steps include height-function setup and successive reductions culminating in an inequality provable by the final multiradial algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper organizes the proof by a sequence of reductions (First Reduction, Second Reduction — Log-volume computations, Third Reduction — Choice of initial 2-data). Each reduction is a subtask: set up heights and arithmetic line bundles, translate the desired inequality into a form amenable to IUT constructions, and choose initial data appropriately so that the multiradial algorithm applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Height functions and arithmetic line bundles (Section 1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and normalization of arithmetic line bundles, arithmetic divisors, degrees, and the associated logarithmic height ht_L : X(Q) → R; properties like additivity of heights and bounded discrepancy classes are established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These foundational definitions and normalizations are prerequisites; many later inequalities are expressed in terms of these heights. The survey emphasizes standard facts (ample generic fiber ⇒ height has growth properties) and sets notation/normalization conventions used throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminaries on Anabelian Geometry (Section 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Background material needed from anabelian geometry: Galois groups of local fields, arithmetic quotients, slimness and commensurable terminality, characterization of cuspidal decomposition groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The survey identifies these anabelian notions as necessary inputs for the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithms; results here are used to reconstruct fields/objects from group-theoretic data (e.g., to obtain cuspidalisations). Validating the proof requires verifying the cited anabelian results (some from Mochizuki's preparatory papers) and their correct application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithms (Section 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms and theorems which reconstruct base fields and function fields (NF-portion) of hyperbolic curves from group-theoretic data; includes elliptic and Belyi cuspidalisations, Uchida's Lemma, and hidden endomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reconstruction procedures are crucial to produce the mono-analytic and arithmetically holomorphic structures used later. The survey highlights the role of 'hidden endomorphisms' and their diagrams in obtaining absolute mono-anabelian results; verifying correctness involves checking each reconstruction step and compatibility with later Kummer/Frobenioid constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean theory / Aut-holomorphic spaces (Section 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Archimedean analogue of mono-anabelian reconstruction: development of aut-holomorphic (orbi)spaces, elliptic cuspidalisation and Kummer theory in the Archimedean setting, and notions of étale-like vs Frobenius-like objects in this theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Archimedean theory is said not to be central, it provides analogues and intuition; its constructions must be consistent with the non-Archimedean ones when used. The survey flags which parts are mainly conceptual versus essential to the main inequality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-volumes and log-shells (Section 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and study of log-volume functions and log-shells associated to local units at non-Archimedean and Archimedean places; these measure local contributions used in global height estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log-volumes play a technical role in bounding heights; computations of log-volumes are a main content of IUTchIV and appear in the Second Reduction. Verifiers should check compatibility of log-volumes with log-links and the multiradial algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminaries on tempered fundamental groups (Section 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions comparing profinite conjugates versus tempered conjugates and related preliminaries on tempered fundamental groups used in reconstruction and evaluation arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tempered vs profinite perspectives are used when passing between topological group reconstructions and Frobenioid/Fundamental-group-theoretic objects. Correct handling of conjugacy indeterminacies and topologies is necessary for later rigidity arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Étale theta function and three fundamental rigidities (Section 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction of the étale theta function and three key rigidities of mono-theta environments: constant multiple rigidity, cyclotomic rigidity, and discrete rigidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each rigidity is used to control indeterminacies in theta values and to enable Kummer theory/multiradiality. The survey points to explicit theorems (e.g., Theorem 7.23 parts (1)-(3)) establishing these rigidities; verification requires checking these rigidity results and their hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenioids theory (Section 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and use of elementary and model Frobenioids, examples, and passage from tempered Frobenioids to mono-theta environments; Frobenioid-theoretic reconstructions and their implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frobenioids provide the categorical framework for Frobenius-like objects and for constructing links (walls) such as the (2)-link and log-link. The survey notes that category-theoretic reconstruction algorithms exist but are not the central technical bottleneck.

rubrics_metrics.name: NF-counterpart of theta evaluation (Section 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of pseudo-monoids of coric functions, cyclotomic rigidity via coric functions, and relationships between (2)-line bundles and (1)-line bundles — i.e., the NF (number-field) counterpart of theta evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This NF-side theory creates the bridge between theta-values (local value groups) and global number-field elements; it is essential for constructing Gaussian monoids and realizing multiradial algorithms globally. Check Kummer-compatibility statements and cyclotomic rigidity results in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hodge theatres (Section 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction of Hodge theatres: initial (2)-data, model objects, NF-Hodge theatres, ell-Hodge theatres, multiplicative and additive symmetries, and bridges (ell- and NF-bridges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hodge theatres are the ambient spaces for Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic evaluation; their symmetries are used to synchronise conjugacy indeterminacies (via Fo-symmetry) and to construct 'good diagonals'. Correct definition and manipulation of Hodge theatres is central to the evaluation maps in Section 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hodge–Arakelov-theoretic evaluation maps (Section 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of radial environments and Hodge-Arakelov evaluation at bad and good places; construction of Gaussian monoids generated by theta values and their role in global constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These evaluation maps translate theta/Frobenioid data into quantitative log-volume/height contributions. The survey emphasizes applications of semi-graph-of-anabelioids consequences (Theorem 6.11) and discrete rigidity to produce Frobenioid-theoretic evaluations; one must check local-to-global compatibilities and bounding arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-links and log-theta-lattices (Section 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of log-links and log-theta-lattices and Kummer-compatible multiradial theta monoids; these are arithmetic analogues of analytic continuation connecting source and target theta-values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log-links are the principal 'walls' that Kummer theory must cross; compatibility of log-links with log-volumes and Kummer correspondences is required for the multiradial algorithm. Verifiers should check definitions (e.g., Definitions 10.8, 12.1, 12.3, 13.9) and the relation with LGP-monoid construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial representation algorithms (Section 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final multiradial algorithms assembling local/global packets, log-Kummer correspondences, theta values acting on log-shells, and number fields acting on log-shells; culminates in the multiradiality theorem (Theorem 13.12) and the height upper bound (Corollary 13.13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the culmination: establish multiradiality (permuting theta values up to mild indeterminacies), compatibility with (2)-link, and use of log-volumes/log-links to derive global height bounds. Checking this requires verifying the three main object constructions (log-shells, theta-values, number fields), canonical splittings of LGP-monoids, and non-interference properties in Propositions 13.6, 13.7, 13.11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclotomic rigidity and Kummer theory protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyclotomic rigidity of mono-theta environments (and of coric functions) protects Kummer theory from bZ(2)-indeterminacies acting on local units, ensuring compatibility of the (2)-link with Kummer portions of the multiradial algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document explains that certain strengthened cyclotomic rigidity (beyond classical local class field theory) is required to obtain multiradial algorithms; verify claims in Propositions 11.4, 12.7, Corollary 12.8 and the dependence on elementary cyclotomic facts (Definition 9.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and canonical splittings of LGP-monoids
rubrics_metrics.description: Using Gaussian monoids and log-links one constructs LGP-monoids equipped with canonical splittings arising from canonical splittings of theta monoids; these splittings are interpreted as non-interference properties in log-Kummer correspondences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propositions 13.6 and 13.7 show existence and properties of LGP-monoids; verifying their canonical splittings and non-interference properties is necessary, since these splittings feed into the final height estimate via the multiradial algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synchronization of conjugacy indeterminacies and 'good diagonals'
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Fo-symmetry in Hodge theatres to synchronise conjugacy indeterminacies and construct 'good diagonals' which lead to horizontally coric objects in the log-theta-lattice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This synchronization (Corollary 11.16(1)) is a technical mechanism used in evaluations to obtain well-defined objects up to the allowed indeterminacies; checking this step is part of the verification of Hodge-Arakelov evaluation and the global assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility requirements across multiple theories
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the argument, compatibility is required among: mono-anabelian reconstructions, Archimedean counterparts, Frobenioid constructions, Kummer correspondences, log-volume computations, and the (2)-link; the final estimate depends on all compatibilities holding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The survey repeatedly notes where compatibilities are used (e.g., compatibility of cyclotomic rigidity with pro-finite topology, compatibility of multiradial algorithms with the (2)-link, and compatibility of log-volumes with log-links). Verification should ensure each inter-theory compatibility claim is established in the referenced preparatory papers or in the constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A motivations and comparison theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: Motivational comparisons: classical de Rham comparison theorem, p-adic Hodge-theoretic comparison theorem, and Hodge-Arakelov-theoretic comparison theorem are given to motivate the (2)-link definition and Hodge-Arakelov evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These appendices give conceptual motivation and show how classical comparison results inspire the arithmetic definitions used; they should be consulted to understand the choice of definitions and the structural parallels used in the proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit bookkeeping: labels, indeterminacies, and processions
rubrics_metrics.description: Because theta-value labels depend on arithmetically holomorphic structure, the framework admits three kinds of mild indeterminacies; processions are used to reduce indeterminacy when transporting labels across a (2)-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final multiradial algorithm allows permutation of theta-values up to mild indeterminacies; the proof requires careful bookkeeping of these indeterminacies and demonstrating they do not affect the height bound beyond bounded discrepancy. Check remarks on processions (Remark 13.1.1) and the bounded-error analyses.
